correctness.rationale: Proved group averaging reduces all real projections to the spectral Fourier projection. The graph gradient is an isometry onto the zero-mean l-infinity hyperplane; quotient duality gives exact finite median formula. The eight-point kernel and norming sign pattern give exact equality; four explicit roots and antiderivative prove continuum median limit 5/pi. The derivative of |D2−1/2| has total variation at most 88, producing the all n Fourier sampling error 44π/(3n²); direct rational inequalities cover n≥21. A standalone exact rational certificate checks each remaining n from 5 to 20 except eight using rigorous π and cosine enclosures, not floating-point evidence. Proof scopes all n≥5 and real scalars.

value.rationale: The first genuinely two-pair Fourier subspace of a finite metric cycle is a natural test of stability for low-harmonic Lipschitz approximation. The result optimizes across every real projection, discovers an exact exceptional finite geometry (n=8), supplies a sharp universal numerical bound and exact continuum limit, and reveals that finite resonance exceeds continuum behavior. These are structural finite-size projection facts rather than a routine reformulation of a single-pair theorem.
